Demand is rows x weight summed over both phases, equal to rows x weight to four decimals here because every domain's anneal weight equals its weight. CONSEQUENCE FOR A CACHE TRUNCATION (de-2): capping a cache at the schedule's own row count binds on the four surplus domains and cannot bind on the five deficit ones, so no domain's distinct-document count changes. Recoverable bytes are 96.9 GB of 165.9 GB, of which zh_web alone is 85 GB. THE EPOCH FIELD IS A CAP, NOT A MULTIPLIER: build_mix's `want = int(rows * frac * weight)` comes from the token budget and never from len(pool), and `epochs` appears only in the cap that binds when len(pool)*epochs < demand.

facts.source: /work/aupai/runs/code_rp1t_neardedup.json via `python3 datagen/near_dedup_scale.py --root data/corpus --domains code_rp1t --out runs/code_rp1t_neardedup.json --ckdir <pod>/runs/code_rp1t_ck --pool 16` (105m52s, exp row code_rp1t_neardedup_0907)

config.method: MinHash-J estimate, n_perm 96, bands 12 x 8 rows, char 5-gram
config.verify: n=200 pairs with est>=0.85, mean est 0.899 vs exact J 0.876, MAE 0.030 -- the estimator reads slightly HIGH, so it over-clusters marginally

facts.uncertainty: Wilson 95% CI given per threshold; the estimate-vs-exact MAE of 0.030 is a separate error term and is not folded into those CIs
facts.boundary: A rate over DOCUMENTS, not tokens. Near-duplicates are not length-neutral, so this does not convert to a token loss by multiplication -- the deduped token count requires building the dir and counting it. It also says nothing about WHICH copy is kept: code_dedup_build keeps the minimum ordinal.

facts.source: /work/aupai/runs/code_rp1t_markup_rate.json (400-doc uniform draw, datagen/sample_markup_rate.py) plus runs/code_rp1t_markup_handread.json (100 code-verdict heads + all 52 positives, hand read by 3b)

config.draw: 400 documents drawn uniformly over code_rp1t's 3,747,157; binomial CI on the doc rate
config.frac_tokens_basis: token-weighted over the SAME 400-doc draw; a ratio estimator, so its error exceeds the binomial CI and no CI is quoted

FP-code.note: C#/Java/TypeScript/PHP source with inline XML doc-comments or Android string resources; the >=20-tags-in-4k rule fires on them

handwritten-web.note: three.js demos, Thymeleaf templates, WordPress walkers, test harness pages -- code we keep

data-xml.note: Android manifests, Atom feeds, DocBook, Qt .ts translations

generated-doc.note: javadoc, dlib cpp_pretty_printer, Xtext -- the only class a filter should target

config.false_negatives: 2 of 100 code-verdict heads were generated markup the sniff missed (an ASF-licensed XML file, a JAXB-generated file); 10 more were prose/README/rst, neither markup nor code
config.classifier: content sniff only -- code_rp1t rows carry {content, source, url} and url is null in 6000 of 6000 sampled, so there is no filename in the domain and extension-based classification is impossible

facts.uncertainty: rate_docs 0.130 is a LOWER BOUND: the sniff misses markup without a doctype or generator line, measured at 2 per 100 code verdicts. The 0.3685 token fraction is NOT removable supply -- three of its four classes are content to keep.
facts.claim: Retracted 2026-09-07 within the hour it was made: '~2.79B tokens of generated markup, the filter is a bigger lever than the dedup by 3.2x'. That multiplied the 36.85% token fraction by the domain total without labelling what was inside it. The hand read shows only 15.9% of those tokens are generated documentation -- 443,264,290, 5.9% of the domain -- against ~864M removed by the th0.9 dedup, so DEDUP is the bigger lever by about 2x and the original claim was inverted.
facts.audit: 3b hand-read all 52 positives and 100 of the 348 code verdicts; 4c ruled no markup filter, and that any future one keys on the generator line, never the tag count
facts.boundary: Says nothing about the OTHER code domains: code_py_starcoder and code_py_rp1t are python-filtered by AST parse, so a generated-HTML population cannot survive there and this rate must not be carried across.
guard_phrases: the markup filter is the bigger lever

Token loss is 17.62% (1,333,065,655) against a DOCUMENT loss of 8.35%: near-duplicate documents are 2.11x the mean length, so a doc rate does not convert to a token loss -- the projection from 11.415% said 6,701,751,475 and was 469,482,734 high, +7.5%, in the direction that flatters supply.
